flashcards.term: Describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for Activity 11.2 (To model lunar phases using a ball, lamp (Sun), and observer (Earth).).
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe the objective, procedure, observation, and principle for activity 11.2 (to model lunar phases using a ball, lamp (sun), and observer (earth).).]
flashcards.definition:
Aim: To model lunar phases using a ball, lamp (Sun), and observer (Earth).
Materials: White plastic ball on stick, Bright unshaded lamp
Steps: Place lamp in center representing Sun. Hold ball at arm length and rotate around body in 8 orbital positions. Observe lit white hemisphere visible from student's eyes.
Observation: Ball appears completely dark between eye and lamp (New Moon) and fully lit when facing away (Full Moon).
Principle: Orbital geometry creates visible lunar phase changes.

flashcards.term: Describe the orbital geometry corresponding to New Moon, First Quarter, and Full Moon phases.
flashcards.phonetic_guide: [Phonetic Guide: describe the orbital geometry corresponding to new moon, first quarter, and full moon phases.]
flashcards.definition: 1. New Moon (Amavasya): Moon lies directly between Sun and Earth. The sunlit half faces away from Earth, rendering it invisible (0% lit). 2. First Quarter: Moon completes 1/4th orbit at 90 deg angle to Earth-Sun line. Half of the illuminated hemisphere is visible (50% lit). 3. Full Moon (Purnima): Earth lies between Sun and Moon. The entire sunlit hemisphere faces Earth, appearing as a complete circular disk (100% lit).
